The products of one region hold many of the same casts. CORA reprocesses
what the NRT products delivered, and the Arctic and the Mediterranean each
have a regional and a global NRT product, built from different streams.
This page asks how much of one product another holds, by matching their
profiles on date and place. The profiles are those ctddump kept after
cleaning and removing duplicates, as on
[Data conversion](analyses-conversion.qmd).

```{ojs}
//| output: false
app = import(new URL("assets/js/app.js", document.baseURI).href)
meta = app.loadAnalyses()
name = (id) => app.datasetName(meta, id)
byDataset = (a, b) => app.datasetOrder(meta, a.dataset_id) - app.datasetOrder(meta, b.dataset_id)
table = app.analysisTable
```

```{ojs}
meta === null ? app.analysesMissing() : html``
```

## NRT and CORA

An NRT product and CORA hold the same casts with different quality
control: the NRT product carries the real time QC done as the data arrived,
CORA the delayed mode QC done since. So CORA should hold every profile of
the NRT products of its region, at least up to its own last profile, and
each cast should have the same observations in both. This section checks
both.

### Coverage: the NRT profiles CORA holds

Each NRT profile is looked for in the CORA of its region. Two profiles are
taken to be the same cast when they share a date and their positions are
within 0.001° of each other in longitude and in latitude (about 100 m or
less). The products rarely store a position to the same last digit, so this
is a tolerance rather than ctddump's
[rounding to three decimals](analyses-conversion.qmd#duplicates-within-a-product), which
misses a pair whose two positions fall either side of a rounding boundary.
Each profile is paired at most once. Each NRT profile is then filed under
the first of these that fits:

- **Outside CORA's period**: dated after CORA's last profile (or before its
  first), so CORA cannot hold it yet. It is left out of the coverage.
- **Same platform code**: CORA has the cast under the same platform code.
- **Another platform code**: CORA has a profile of the same date and place
  under a different code, among the profiles not yet paired.
- **Nearby, not paired**: CORA has a profile of the same platform and date
  within 0.01° (about 1 km). Probably the same cast with its position
  stored differently, but not counted as found.
- **Platform in CORA, cast not**: CORA has the platform, not this cast.
- **Platform not in CORA**: CORA has nothing under this platform code.

The coverage is the share found, under the same code or another, of the
profiles in CORA's period.

```{ojs}
meta ? app.analysisFigure(
  "conversion_coverage",
  "Where the NRT profiles dated within CORA's period were found in the CORA of their region. The figure on each bar is the coverage: the share found under the same platform code or another. The number of profiles in CORA's period is in brackets.",
  "Stacked bars per NRT product of its profiles by whether and how CORA holds them."
) : html``
```

```{ojs}
coverage = meta ? app.loadAnalysisTable("conversion_coverage") : null
share = (v, r) => `${app.formatCount(v)} (${app.formatShare(v, r.n_inside)})`
meta ? table((coverage ?? []).map((r) => ({
  ...r,
  key: `${r.dataset_id}|${r.compared_id}`,
  n_inside: r.n_profiles - r.n_outside_period,
  n_found: r.n_same_platform + r.n_other_platform
})).sort(byDataset), [
  { key: "dataset_id", label: "Product", align: "left", format: name },
  { key: "period_end", label: "CORA's period", align: "left", title: "The dates of CORA's first and last profiles in the region", format: (v, r) => `${r.period_start} to ${v}` },
  { key: "n_profiles", label: "Profiles" },
  { key: "n_outside_period", label: "Outside the period" },
  { key: "n_inside", label: "In the period" },
  { key: "n_found", label: "Coverage", title: "Found in CORA under the same platform code or another, as a share of the profiles in CORA's period", format: share },
  { key: "n_same_platform", label: "Same code", format: share },
  { key: "n_other_platform", label: "Another code", format: share },
  { key: "n_nearby", label: "Nearby", format: share },
  { key: "n_platform_only", label: "Platform in CORA, cast not", format: share },
  { key: "n_no_platform", label: "Platform not in CORA", format: share }
]) : html``
```

Year by year, the same classes show when the gaps are:

```{ojs}
meta ? app.analysisFigure(
  "conversion_coverage_years",
  "The NRT profiles of each year by whether and how the CORA of their region holds them, the years after CORA's last profile in grey. Each panel has its own scale.",
  "Stacked bars per NRT product and year of its profiles by whether and how CORA holds them."
) : html``
```

What the coverage shows:

- **The Mediterranean regional product is in CORA in full**, under the same
  platform codes.
- **The Arctic regional product is almost entirely in CORA.** Most of it is
  under the same codes. Ice-tethered profilers go by their own number in
  the NRT product and by a WMO number in CORA, so they are found under
  another code. The little that is missing is split between nearby
  profiles, casts CORA lacks on platforms it has (some platforms' records
  in CORA end earlier than in NRT), and platforms CORA does not have.
- **The Arctic part of the global product is in CORA too, a large part of
  it under other codes**, especially in recent years. The naming goes the
  other way here: the profilers have a WMO number in the NRT product and
  their own number in CORA, and a fixed station has a name in one and a
  number in the other.
- **The Baltic product holds many profiles from platforms CORA does not
  have at all**, most of them from the 1990s and 2000s. These are casts
  CORA has not taken in, rather than casts it holds under another name:
  the match on date and place alone finds little more.
- **The Mediterranean part of the global product is mostly in CORA.** The
  largest gap is one platform in one recent year, a platform CORA has
  otherwise.

### The pairs hold the same observations

A pair is one cast in two versions. CORA's reprocessing reviews its flags,
but the cast should keep its observations, so the two versions should hold
the same number of them. Under the same platform code, nearly every pair
does. Under another code, many do not, the Arctic profilers above all:
the two products carry these instruments' records sampled at different
levels, so they are the same casts in different versions rather than
copies.

```{ojs}
matches = meta ? app.loadAnalysisTable("conversion_match") : null
pairShare = (v, r) => `${app.formatCount(v)} (${app.formatShare(v, r.n_matched)})`
meta ? table((matches ?? []).map((r) => ({ ...r, key: `${r.dataset_id}|${r.compared_id}|${r.coverage}` })).sort(byDataset), [
  { key: "dataset_id", label: "Product", align: "left", format: name },
  { key: "coverage", label: "Platform code", align: "left", format: (v) => (v === "same_platform" ? "Same" : "Another") },
  { key: "n_matched", label: "Pairs" },
  { key: "n_same_obs", label: "Same observations", format: pairShare },
  { key: "n_more_in_dataset", label: "NRT has more", format: pairShare },
  { key: "n_more_in_compared", label: "CORA has more", format: pairShare }
]) : html``
```

## Overlap between NRT products

The Arctic and the Mediterranean each have a regional and a global NRT
product, built from different streams. The same match as above, on date
and place, says how much of one the other holds too. The two share no
platform code, so only the match without it can find what they have in
common; where it finds little, the two products hold different casts
rather than the same casts under different names.

```{ojs}
overlap = meta ? app.loadAnalysisTable("conversion_overlap") : null
isCora = (id) => (meta?.datasets ?? []).find((d) => d.id === id)?.product === "CORA"
meta ? table((overlap ?? []).filter((r) => !isCora(r.dataset_id) && !isCora(r.compared_id))
  .map((r) => ({ ...r, key: `${r.dataset_id}|${r.compared_id}` })), [
  { key: "dataset_id", label: "Product", align: "left", format: name },
  { key: "compared_id", label: "Also in", align: "left", format: name },
  { key: "n_profiles", label: "Profiles" },
  { key: "n_matched_same_platform", label: "Same platform code", format: (v, r) => `${app.formatCount(v)} (${app.formatShare(v, r.n_profiles)})` },
  { key: "n_matched_any_platform", label: "On date and place", format: (v, r) => `${app.formatCount(v)} (${app.formatShare(v, r.n_profiles)})` }
]) : html``
```
